main_body: Snow ground patch, a repeating tile of pale blue-white snow drifts and dark grey-green patches (rock/grass) with speckle, covering 4x3 tiles
top_band: none - terrain ground tile, no standing object; the surface is a flat repeating pattern
evidence: This is a terrain ground tile, not a standing object, so the 3/4 top-plus-front contract does not apply. It reads as a seamless ground surface with no standing volume, no side faces and no elevation drawing. The terrain kind matches the content.

style.evidence: The candidate has about 5 lightness steps: white, pale blue, mid blue-grey, grey-green and dark green-grey. The dark patches carry good speckle. The pale snow regions are large flat fills of one or two near-white colours, with areas well over 5x5 px and little grain, unlike the grass and paving references, which vary across the surface. The pattern repeats obviously every tile (identical blobs and white dots), which looks mechanical and makes the patch read as a wallpaper. There are no outlines, so no sticker look. Tile density is slightly lower than the references because the snow tiles are mostly 2-3 colours. Flat fills in the snow areas and the obvious repetition make it thinner than the references.
